'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Odesa strikes (2022–present)|Odesa strikes]]
***Two [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[ballistic missile]]s strike the port city of [[Odesa]], killing three people and injuring sixteen others. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-missile-kills-three-ukrainian-port-odesa-2024-05-01/ (Reuters)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/missile-strikes-ukrainian-port-odesa-13-injured-regional-governor-says-2024-05-01/ (Reuters 2)] [https://www.kyivpost.com/post/31925 (''Kyiv Post'')]
**[[Russia]] displays captured [[NATO]] military vehicles and equipment at an open-air exhibition in Victory Park on [[Poklonnaya Hill]] in Moscow. Among the captured vehicles are a [[Germany|German]] [[Leopard 2]] tank and an [[United States|American]] [[M1 Abrams]] tank. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-68934205 (BBC News)] [https://www.foxnews.com/world/russias-kremlin-parades-western-equipment-captured-ukrainian-army-exhibition (Fox News)]
*[[Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Israeli invasion of the Gaza Strip (2023–present)|Israeli invasion of Gaza]], [[Humanitarian aid during the Israel–Hamas war]]
***Amid pressure from the [[United States]], [[Israel]] reopens the [[Erez Crossing|Erez-Beit Hanoun Crossing]] and allows [[Humanitarian aid|aid trucks]] into the northern part of the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israel-allows-trucks-newly-reopened-erez-crossing-into-gaza-after-us-pressure-2024-05-01/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents''' 
*[[2024 Guangdong floods]]
**Forty-eight people are killed and 30 more injured as twenty-three vehicles fell down during a [[highway]] collapse in [[Meizhou]], [[Guangdong]], [[China]]. [https://apnews.com/article/china-highway-collapse-guangdong-meizhou-9cf1836ea73ebc008ee6fcaeed942f51 (AP)]
*[[2024 Kenya floods]]
**The death toll from ongoing flooding in [[Kenya]] increases to 181, as more homes and roads are destroyed. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/kenya-flood-toll-rises-179-homes-roads-are-destroyed-2024-05-01/ (Reuters)]
*[[2024 Rio Grande do Sul floods]]
**Ten people are killed by heavy rain in [[Rio Grande do Sul]], [[Brazil]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/heavy-rains-brazils-south-kill-8-people-leave-109827342 (ABC News)]
*[[2024 Indian heat wave]]
**At least nine people are killed in an ongoing [[heatwave]] in [[East India|eastern India]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/india/india-likely-see-above-normal-maximum-temperatures-may-weather-office-says-2024-05-01/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Colombia–Israel relations]]
***[[President of Colombia|President]] [[Gustavo Petro]] announces that [[Colombia]] will suspend diplomatic relations with Israel over its actions in Gaza. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/colombia-president-petro-says-will-break-diplomatic-relations-with-israel-2024-05-01/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Rwanda asylum plan]]
**[[United Kingdom|British]] authorities begin detaining migrants ahead of [[deportation]] flights to [[Rwanda]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/uk-begins-detaining-migrants-set-be-deported-rwanda-2024-05-01/ (Reuters)]
**[[Republic of Ireland|Irish]] [[Taoiseach]] [[Simon Harris]] announces the deployment of 100 [[Garda Síochána|police officers]] to [[Republic of Ireland–United Kingdom border|the border]] with [[Northern Ireland]] amid fears that thousands of migrants might flee the UK in order to avoid deportation to Rwanda. Ireland also declares the United Kingdom a "safe country" so that asylum seekers can be deported back to the UK. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2024/05/01/sunak-dont-send-police-to-irish-border-to-stop-migrants/ (''The Telegraph'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/czq588jqz8lo (BBC News)]
*[[Abortion in North Carolina]]
**[[U.S.]] federal judge [[Catherine Eagles]] blocks several of [[North Carolina]]'s restrictions on the abortion pill [[mifepristone]], striking down a requirement that the drug can only be prescribed by doctors in-person, as well as a requirement for patients to have an in-person follow-up appointment. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-judge-blocks-some-north-carolina-restrictions-abortion-pill-2024-05-01/ (Reuters)]
*A student is fatally shot by police officers outside [[Mount Horeb Area School District|Mount Horeb Middle School]] in [[Mount Horeb, Wisconsin|Mount Horeb]], [[Wisconsin]], United States, after the police received reports of someone carrying a weapon. [https://apnews.com/article/wisconsin-mount-horeb-active-shooter-school-8f1a4cb9b428eb4cb863469492625dfd (AP)]
*At least 217 people are detained by [[General Directorate of Security (Turkey)|Turkish police]] during [[International Workers' Day|May Day]] rallies in [[Istanbul]], after police fire tear gas and rubber bullets into the crowds. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkish-police-fire-tear-gas-detain-dozens-may-day-protesters-istanbul-2024-05-01/ (Reuters)]
*At least 45 people are arrested and 12 police officers are injured at [[International Workers' Day|May Day]] protests in [[Paris]]. [[National Police (France)|French police]] use [[tear gas]] and batons to disperse several protests. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/riot-police-protesters-clash-paris-during-may-day-protests-2024-05-01/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Israel–Hamas war protests]]
**[[2024 pro-Palestinian protests on university campuses]] 
***[[2024 University of California, Los Angeles pro-Palestinian campus occupation]]
****Pro-Israel counter-protestors attack the pro-Palestinian encampment at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], throwing objects and attempting to destroy barricades. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/police-move-quell-clashes-los-angeles-pro-palestinian-campus-protest-2024-05-01/ (Reuters)]
***The administration of [[Shiraz University]] in [[Southern Iran]] offers free tuition to college students in the United States who have been expelled for participating in anti-Israel campus protests. [https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/389331 (Arutz Shiva)]
*[[2024 Scottish government crisis]]
**The [[Scottish National Party]] administration survives the [[vote of no confidence]] earlier this week, prompting the party to seek a replacement for outgoing [[First Minister of Scotland|First Minister]] [[Humza Yousaf]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2024/5/1/scottish-government-survives-confidence-vote-after-hamza-yusuf-quits (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Homosexuality and Methodism]]
**The [[United Methodist Church]] votes 692–51 to repeal a longstanding ban on [[LGBT clergy in Christianity|LGBTQ clergy]] while additionally prohibiting [[District superintendent (Methodism)|superintendents]] from forbidding a [[Same-sex marriage|same-sex wedding]]. [https://apnews.com/article/united-methodist-lgbtq-clergy-general-conference-acabe18fe22b6838e3005ad8895534fa (AP)]
